newsitem.title: FRANCE: Jet Services profits dip but turnover up.
newsitem.headline: Jet Services profits dip but turnover up.

text.p: French road and air express distribution company Jet Services made net profits of 45 million francs for the financial year ending March 31 1997 compared to 71 million francs in 1995/6.
Turnover rose 7.7 percent to 1.69 billion francs "despite unfavourable market conditions and in particular strong downward pressures on express rates," the company added.
Global traffic reached an average daily volume of 201,045 documents and parcels, up 11 percent on 1995/96.
The group invested 72 million francs in 1996/97 in extending its intra-European express network, upgrading IT facilities and increasing its sales staff in Europe.
The 1997/98 financial year should see turnover surpass two billion francs. The company's financial strategy was an introduction on the French stock exchange in the next one to two years.

Jet Services chief executive officer Roger Caille told a press conference it is considering two sites for the transfer of the group's Paris/CDG air cargo hub - Dole, a little-used airfield situated in centre-east France and Lyon-Satolas airport. However, there was still a chance it would maintain the hub at CDG.

Previously it has said it wanted to develop air cargo services between France and southern Europe as CDG is a little too far north to be an ideal location. - Reuters Air Cargo Service Tel+ 44 171 542 7706 Fax +5017 - www.racs.com
